answers.reason: The chancellor holds a high central office and is involved in university-wide matters.
The chancellor heads the central administration and is responsible for the budget.
Appointments are part of the university-wide plan involving office holders of higher rank.
The faculty council handles faculty-specific affairs, but the chancellor holds a higher central office.
Study programmes are treated as part of the university-wide plan involving higher office holders.
Examination matters of individual students are handled at the faculty or board level without chancellor participation.
Internal research funding is an internal faculty matter handled below the central administration level.
Module revisions are handled at the program level without the chancellor's direct involvement.
Laboratory equipment procurement is a specific faculty-level task not involving higher central office holders.
Orientation week planning is an administrative matter for students and faculty members rather than the chancellor.
